title: Versioned model I/O contracts and performance snapshotting
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, machine-checkable contract for onboarding and pinning model versions that covers: (1) canonical prompt/input schema and versioning rules, (2) expected output shape and semantics, (3) runtime parameter semantics (top_p, temperature, streaming boundaries), and (4) a performance snapshot artifact (latency P50/P95, throughput at representative batch sizes, tokenization delta) that is published alongside a pinned model entry. The contract must be strict enough to detect breaking changes during model upgrades (or accidental drift) and loose enough to allow micro-optimizations (kernel swaps, quantization) that do not change functional I/O. Deliverables: contract spec doc, JSON schema + validator used during onboarding, CI checks that fail model onboarding/rollout on breaking changes, tooling to capture and publish perf snapshots to the model catalog, console UI hooks to display perf artifacts and a checksum of tokenizer + config. Scope excludes: policy/content changes, training-time behavior beyond deterministic I/O for same seed/config.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Canonical input schema v1 defined (prompt envelope, metadata fields, allowed attachments) and stored in repo as JSON Schema.
A2: Output shape spec (primary text, structured blocks, function-call tokens) defined with examples for interplay with function/tool calling.
A3: SDK validator integrated into onboarding CLI that rejects pinned-model uploads if schema mismatch is detected unless explicit compatibility waiver is provided.
A4: Performance snapshot format (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, throughput@batch-sizes, memory footprint, tokenizer tokenization delta) standardized and generated by onboarding benchmark harness.
A5: Model catalog UI exposes perf snapshot and tokenizer checksum; rollout guard rejects canary >10% latency regression automatically unless overridden with signed review.
A6: End-to-end CI test included in model-onboard pipeline: baseline vs candidate model run on 100 representative prompts — diffs reported and regressions flagged.
A7: Documentation and a short runbook for support/SE explaining common causes of false positives (tokenizer updates, numeric nondeterminism) and mitigation steps.
A8: Unit and integration tests for validator + perf snapshot generator with >80% coverage for code paths used during onboarding.
A9: Backwards-compatibility policy documented: additive changes allowed for prompt schema, breaking changes require new major version and migration notes.
technical_notes: Use content-addressable checksum (sha256) of tokenizer files + model config JSON to detect tokenization drift instead of relying solely on model hash.
Perf snapshot runner should be deterministic: fixed seed, pinned hardware profile, warmup tokens and fixed prompt set sampled from customer-like workloads.
Tolerance thresholds: default P95 latency regression tolerance = +5% for minor patch updates, +0% for major pinned upgrades unless explicitly approved.
Validator implementation: JSON Schema for prompt envelope + a deterministic 'shape comparator' for outputs that tolerates order-insensitive fields and floating-number epsilon differences.

Runtime enforcement: the serving layer should annotate requests that declare a legacy prompt_version and route to compatibility shim where possible; otherwise return structured 409 with migration hints.
Publish artifacts to model-catalog S3 bucket with stable key pattern: /models/{model_id}/pins/{pin_id}/contract-v{n}/perf-snapshot-{timestamp}.json
Integration points: onboarding CLI (ml-onboard), model-catalog API, runtime admission controller, console model detail page, and the rollout service (canary manager).
